_notes: POPPER_PLAN.md item B2. kappa and alpha are fixed here rather than per entry so that a change is one visible diff; choosing either after seeing a p-value voids the calibration. relevance_threshold is POPPER's r0, on the paper's Listing-4 rubric (0.1 irrelevant .. 1.0 highly relevant); 0.6 is 'moderately relevant' and is the floor for a prediction whose e-value may enter a claim's product. 'evaluable' is set by the claims/EVALUABILITY.md audit and gates core/adjudication.py: only 'e-value' entries may contribute.

predictions.statement: Trained cluster centroids are closer to a spherical t-design than step-0 centroids: low-order Gegenbauer moments smaller.
predictions.h0: Trained and step-0 centroids are equally far from a spherical t-design.
predictions.h1: Trained centroids have smaller low-order Gegenbauer moments.
predictions.falsifier: No difference between trained and step-0 => the repulsive-limit story is unsupported.
predictions.instrument: 1c-F (p1c_frames/design_test.py, centroids.py)
predictions.null_construction: Monte-Carlo permutation against a matched i.i.d. baseline at the trained configuration's own (m, d). STATISTIC, fixed in advance: the sum over degrees k=1..3 of the (step0 - trained) Q_k ratio, each standardised by that degree's own null standard deviation. ALTERNATIVE: one-sided 'greater' (P-S1 predicts trained ratios SMALLER, so step0 - trained > 0). NULL: two independent i.i.d. configurations at the same (m, d), same statistic -- a pair per draw, so the null carries both arms' sampling variability. Resolution floor 1/(n_draws+1). Implemented in p1c_frames/centroids.py::p_value_p_s1.
predictions.notes: E[Q_k] = 1/n exactly for i.i.d. points, so an ABSOLUTE threshold makes every large-n configuration read as a design (UPDATE_PLAN.md 5.7). The ratio is the adjudicated quantity, not Q_k. NULL CONSTRUCTION SHARPENED 2026-08-23, before any adjudication. The registered falsifier ('no difference') and the direction are unchanged; what is added is the multi-degree combination rule and the one-sided direction, neither of which the original wording fixed. Both had to be settled before running, because choosing a combination rule after seeing three per-degree results is itself a selection. Standardising by each degree's null sd is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: UPDATE_PLAN.md 5.8 measured the band narrowing from ~0.17 at k=1 to ~0.002 at k=3, so an unstandardised sum is dominated by k=1 and discards the degrees that are more sensitive in relative terms -- the same error 5.8 records having made once already. Calibration verified on synthetic null-vs-null pairs (frac p<=0.05 at nominal); power 88% at alpha=0.05 against a simplex-like configuration; reversed arms give p=1.000, confirming the one-sidedness.

predictions.statement: Two steering vectors of EQUAL NORM whose V-eigenbasis decompositions are predominantly attractive (U_pos) versus predominantly repulsive (U_neg), injected at the same layer, produce OPPOSITE-SIGNED changes in the effective rank of the token population at that layer.
predictions.h0: The sign of the effective-rank change is independent of the vector's U_pos/U_neg decomposition: at matched norm, both arms move effective rank in the same direction (or neither moves it).
predictions.h1: Sign of the effective-rank change tracks the decomposition: attractive-dominant steering reduces effective rank, repulsive-dominant steering increases it.
predictions.falsifier: Both arms move effective rank the same way, or the effect tracks ||s|| and is insensitive to the decomposition. Either says the impulse reading adds nothing over 'a vector was added'.
predictions.instrument: 7-steering: core/intervention.py injection; p7_motifs/interaction_graph.py for edge sign; core/metrics.py effective_rank
predictions.null_construction: Two-sample comparison of the signed effective-rank delta between the two arms, over a set of matched-norm vector pairs drawn per layer. The null is generated by the SAME injection procedure with the decomposition label permuted across pairs, so the norm, the layer and the injection machinery are all held fixed and only the label moves. Requires the pair-drawing scheme (how many pairs, how 'predominantly' is thresholded) fixed in advance.
predictions.notes: NORM MATCHING IS THE DESIGN, not a nicety: without it the comparison is confounded by exactly the quantity the standard account predicts from. Run this one first -- it is the only bridge entry where the two accounts make INCOMPATIBLE rather than merely different predictions, and it needs no new instrument. Phase 7's steering entry asks 'which edges change sign under it, and does a new hub form?' -- this prediction supplies the falsifiable half that entry needs, and the norm-matching is the design: without it the comparison is confounded by exactly the quantity the standard account predicts from. Phase 7's note that archive/p3_crosscoder/steering.py already implements a steering intervention with a recorded null applies here and should be read before building.

predictions.h1: Divergence grows superlinearly in remaining depth.
predictions.falsifier: Divergence flat in remaining depth, or growing linearly, across ablation points.

predictions.null_construction: Growth-exponent comparison against a MATCHED RANDOM-DIRECTION ablation of equal magnitude at the same layer -- the same control design design-5c.md already requires for its force-collapse and force-disperse arms. Permutation over ablation points once the fitted exponent is the statistic.

Sits under Phase 7's 'activation patching' entry, whose recapture-vs-propagation framing is the same question asked about basins: superlinear divergence in remaining depth IS propagation, flat divergence IS recapture. The matched random-direction control at equal magnitude is required, not optional.

_status_notes: status: 'active' | 'dormant'. Dormant means the prediction stands -- it was pre-registered, its falsifier is unchanged, and it has NOT been withdrawn -- but no live instrument can currently adjudicate it, so core/adjudication.py refuses it and it contributes nothing to its claim's E. Orthogonal to 'evaluable', which is about whether a valid null exists: a prediction can be e-value AND dormant (the null is sound, the apparatus is gone). Reversible on reintroduction, which is why it is a status rather than a deletion.
